paragraphs: Mia's Fact File: The Camel, posted by Mia. Last Saturday, the Explorers saw a camel at a small zoo. Teacher Kim reads each post first, so I checked every fact twice. I love animals, so I wrote this page with a big smile. Is it possible to live in a hot desert? The camel says yes!

Size: it is about two meters tall, and it is very heavy. A big camel weighs almost five hundred kilos. Food: it eats grass, leaves, and small plants. Home: it lives in the desert, where the sand is hot and dry. Life: a camel lives for about forty years. Camels are wild animals, but many live with people. A mother camel has one baby at a time. A baby camel can stand after a few hours.

Its pale fur is the color of sand. The fur keeps the camel cool during the day and warm at night. It has long eyelashes, and they keep the sand out of its eyes. Its knees have thick skin, and the skin is hard like leather. This is special, because the camel sits on hot sand. Its wide feet do not go deep into the sand. It can close its nose when the wind is full of sand.

The hump is a special part of the camel. It is full of fat, not water. When the camel has no food, it uses the fat. A camel can walk for many days without water. Then it can drink about one hundred liters in a few minutes. That is possible because its body is very strong. People make bags and shoes from camel leather. The camel is not as fast as a horse, but it can walk for many more days.

I put the best photo on the blog. The camel looked at me and moved its mouth slowly. It is a gentle animal. I like it very much. Lily said, "It looks very calm." Which animal do you want to see at the zoo? Tell us in a message!
